shots.phrase: Begin by framing Program Overview and Credit Status as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Consider this worked case: A student enrolled in the summer co-op program receives full-time enrollment credits for housing, financial aid, and academic advising purposes.
'Summer Co-op' with a highlighted badge stating 'Full-Time Status' under the co-op column.
Now define Summer Term Registration Requirements precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: A student schedules a 12-week summer placement with a weekly commitment of exactly 35 hours to meet the minimum threshold.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how Prerequisite Coursework operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: A student verifies their transcript shows a passing grade in CSCI-099 before submitting the summer co-op registration form.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in Student Work Report Requirement and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: A student submits a structured PDF report detailing project scope, technical challenges, and deliverables after the summer term.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Supervisor Evaluation Process to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: A supervisor completes a standardized form rating the student's technical contributions, communication, and professional conduct.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Grading Consistency Standard, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: The academic advisor reviews both documents and confirms that the student's self-assessment aligns with the supervisor's ratings before finalizing the grade.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around ACM Ethical Practice in Co-op with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Consider this worked case: A co-op student implements robust security measures and documents all code changes to ensure transparency and prevent unintended system harm.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Responsible Technical Communication to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Consider this worked case: A student's co-op report includes a literature review section that explicitly cites prior research and clearly separates empirical results from theoretical claims.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Research Integrity and Documentation to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: A student maintains version-controlled code repositories and detailed methodology notes so that their co-op project can be independently verified.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Consider this worked case: A student uses a final checklist to confirm 12-week/35-hour commitment, report-supervisor alignment, and ACM ethical standards before submitting grades.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
